description: Post a batch of messages to Slack channels. Each message names its own channel_id and text, and may set thread_ts to reply inside a thread. Messages for the same channel are sent in order. Every message gets its own result row, so one failure never stops the rest.

response_schema.description: chat.postMessage. Lenient on purpose: the echoed message carries many more fields.

quirks: Slack answers HTTP 200 with {ok:false, error} for its own failures. execute.ts turns ok=false into the connector error contract and puts it on that message's own result row, so a refused message is never reported as sent.
chat.postMessage posts ONE message. Slack has no batch endpoint for it, so the plural contract runs as bounded concurrent singles.

Slack accepts about one message per SECOND per channel, and does not queue different channels behind each other. So the fan-out unit is the CHANNEL, not the message: messages are grouped by channel_id, one worker sends each group in the caller's order, and two messages for the same channel never overlap.
The app-wide rate limit bucket cannot express a per-channel rule, which is why the grouping lives in the node.

channel_id.description: The channel id to post in, such as C012AB3CD. A user id posts a direct message.

thread_ts.description: The parent message's ts. Set it to reply inside that thread.

results.description: One row per input message, in the caller's order.

index.description: The message's position in the caller's messages array.

message_ts.description: The posted message's timestamp id. Use it as thread_ts to reply to it.
